# ADR-079: Non-prod role + signing secrets are generated by the Pulumi program itself

- **Status:** Proposed
- **Date:** 2026-10-04
- **Ticket:** OPS.1
- **Requirement ids:** REQ-ARCH-30, REQ-SPEC-30, REQ-ARCH-38
- **Spec:** §13.2

## Context
Every non-prod stack historically needed an operator to hand-set `rhema:*DatabaseUrl` encrypted
configs and hand-`ALTER ROLE` the SEC.1 role split before services could boot — a two-pass
ceremony no unattended `pr-<n>` lifecycle can afford, and one of the reasons `dev` stayed a
skeleton. The standing posture "secret values are operator-provided out of band" protects prod's
material but over-constrains fresh stacks whose credentials are disposable by definition.

## Decision
On non-prod stacks (`dev`, `pr-<n>`) `infra/pulumi/index.ts` mints the full generated set —
`NONPROD_GENERATED_SECRET_IDS` in `stages.ts`: the postgres bootstrap password, the
`rhema_app_login` + `rhema_collab` DSNs, the composed `postgres`-role `system-database-url`, the
RS256 `run-token-signing-key` (`@pulumi/tls`, stable across `up`s), `better-auth-secret`, and
`email-action-secret` (`@pulumi/random`, `special:false` for URL-inlined material) — and writes
them as Secret Manager **versions** on the stack-local containers. `system-database-url`'s
container is provisioned via `extraIds` so prod's `ALL_SECRET_IDS` set stays byte-identical.
Values exist **only** in encrypted Pulumi state + Secret Manager; services mount them by
`secretKeyRef`; nothing is logged, exported plaintext, or committed. On prod the entire block is
skipped — prod's secrets stay operator-seeded and its `app-database-url` keeps the SEC.1
generated-version + operator-ALTER ceremony (OPS.2's adoption scope, untouched here).

## Consequences
- `pulumi up` on a fresh non-prod stack is self-contained: no hand configs, no ALTER pass — the
  migrate Job (ADR-078) turns the generated passwords live.
- `pulumi destroy`/`stack rm` removes the whole credential set with the stack — zero orphaned
  secrets, satisfying the lifecycle acceptance criterion by construction.
- Encrypted Pulumi state becomes a system-of-record for non-prod credentials; state access is
  therefore a security boundary (it already was — Pulumi secret outputs are encrypted at rest).
- Generated values rotate if the `RandomPassword`/`PrivateKey` resources are replaced; the
  run-token key is `@pulumi/tls` so plain `up`s do not rotate it.

## Alternatives considered
- **Operator-seeded secrets per preview:** rejected — recreates the hand ceremony the guard exists
  to remove, and invites stale `rhema-prod-*` values being pasted into previews (REQ-ARCH-38).
- **Secret Manager auto-generation (`secret-manager` gcloud flows / GCP-side rotation):** rejected —
  versions still must be written; doing it in-program keeps one audited write path and lets the
  DSN compose the password the migrate Job needs.
- **Plaintext `value:` envs for disposables:** rejected — REQ-ARCH-30 makes no stage exception for
  secret-in-env.

## Revisit trigger
If state exfiltration becomes a concern (shared backend access), revisit a KMS-wrapped or
operator-seeded hybrid; if previews ever need real third-party material, that decision supersedes
this one's scope.
